root_idea.summary: The root centers on mixing: bringing one substance into another so that they are blended.
root_idea.development: The basic idea of physical blending extends to names for admixtures and blended substances, and figuratively to adulteration, confusion, dishonesty, and mixed multitudes.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The sole supplied Quranic form group is presented under the normalized noun citation form شَوْبٌ.

senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression لَشَوْبًا مِنْ حَمِيمٍ, it denotes a mixture or admixture of boiling water. The supplied Quran occurrence is 37:67:5.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To mix one thing with another, especially liquids such as milk or honey with water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form I verb describing physical mingling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To adulterate, vitiate, or sophisticate something by mixing another substance into it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or evaluative extension of physical mixing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To mix up or confound speech or actions; idiomatically, to act inconsistently or defend without energy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of disordered or inconsistent conduct and speech.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To act treacherously or unfaithfully; to lie, deceive in buying or selling, or deal insincerely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative ethical and commercial use of the verb.
Intransitive Form VIII usage describing a state of mixture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mixture of water or milk with another substance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete food or drink mixture, especially something blended with water or milk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Honey used as an admixture in beverages; also honey regarded as mixed with wax.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may designate honey because it is used to blend drinks or is associated with admixture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression لَا شَوْبَ وَلَا رَوْبَ, mixing or dishonesty in a sale, and hence a disclaimer of responsibility for defects.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression concerning the absence of adulteration, insincerity, or liability for a faulty commodity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A medley or mixed multitude of sundry sorts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Plural usage for a heterogeneous group.
A noun for an element or instance of deceptive conduct.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A virgin bride on the night of consummation, or that night itself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression بِلَيْلَةِ شَيْبَاءَ or related expressions for the night of a bride’s first consummation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A streak or admixture of whiteness against the darkness of night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized descriptive noun, treated in the evidence as the singular of شَوَائِبُ in this sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A trace or element of ownership or right mixed into a matter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A legal or figurative use for even a small claim, interest, or qualifying element.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An impurity, contaminant, pollution, or foul thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used as the singular of شَوَائِبُ in the sense of polluting or unclean elements.
A passive participial adjective, including mixtures of food or liquid with additional ingredients.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A variegated case or cover for a flask or bottle; in the plural, palm-leaf receptacles.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is associated with mixing because of its red, yellow, and green coloration; the plural may have the receptacle sense.

cautions: The attribution of شَيْبَاءُ to شوب is disputed in the evidence; it may instead be connected with شِيبٌ. The item is retained with that qualification.
The Quran example uses the independently supplied QAC location 37:67:5; historical citation notation elsewhere is not converted into a modern verse location.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The derivation of شَيْبَاءُ from شوب versus شيب remains unresolved, although its lexical definition and usage are represented under the cautious Classical entry.
